newsitem.title: USA: U.S. light crudes rise late on refiner demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. light crudes rise late on refiner demand.

text.p: U.S. light, sweet crudes made further gains in moderate trade Friday underpinned by a lack of foreign supplies and buoyant refiner demand.
Louisiana light and heavy grades again performed bullishly although heavier grades succumbed to some selling pressure.

"It's not quite clear why Heavy Louisiana Sweet is gaining over LLS (Light Louisisna Sweet), but there are pockets of demand due to the distillate squeeze," an East Coast trader said, citing a possible move by refiners to increase heating oil production after a meeting between Energy Secretary Hazel O-Leary and oil industry executives on Friday.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $25.75-85 a barrel, up about 35 cents from Thursday.
The Nov/Dec WTI spread widening to 45 cents, up five cents from the morning, aided a rise in WTI/Cushing Posting Plus pushing it up to postings plus $2.15 a barrel from $2.09.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James inched up to plus 69 cents a barrel, up five cents from early in the day, with Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire hitting plus 72 cents, up three cents.
Heavy grades were softer, with one refiner in Kansas seen selling parcels of West Texas Sour/Midland which brought the grade down to WTI minus $1.44 a barrel, down two cents.
Speculation was that the refiner had access to U.S. West Coast grades and was backing out supplies.
Canadian heavy crudes were also seen displacing some amount of domestic sour barrels in the Midwest.
